title: Relative profinite free modules and the unbounded derived slice Hom identity
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site in compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $p_X$ be the condensed-point morphism [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], and put $B=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], K-injective total right derived direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a profinite set $P$, put $U=X[P]$, with projection $\rho:U\to X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], and write $h_P(Q)=C(Q,P)$ and $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. Let $A=\Lambda[P]$ be the free internal module on $h_P$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]; similarly $B[h_U]$ means the left adjoint of forgetting $B$-modules to sheaves of sets, applied to $h_U$.

There are canonical generator-preserving identifications
$$p_X^{-1}h_P\cong h_U,\qquad p_X^*A\cong B[h_U].$$
For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ there is a canonical isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category
$$\gamma_{X,P,K}:R\mathcal Hom_B(p_X^*A,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\rho_*\rho^*K.$$
Here $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is identified with the slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The normalization of $\gamma$ is the free-generator evaluation: for a K-injective representative $J$ of $K$ and any test $V\to X$, its representative is the identification $\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],J)(V)=J(V\times_XU)$ with the unchanged differential. This specifies an isomorphism of derived objects, not merely of their cohomology groups. It is natural in $K$. The internal-module isomorphism and this section-ring description agree under the canonical equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], with its tensor and evaluation normalizations [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison, lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison, lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. In particular, for every $N\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda})$, $\rho^*p_X^*N=p_U^*N$ under the canonical pullback-composition comparison.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open) and 08J7 (section-internal-hom); agent free-generator slice calculation. Profinite representability: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Example 3.1 and (4.1).

proof.text: The functor $u_X:Q\mapsto X[Q]$ preserves finite limits and covers by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Thus its sheaf inverse image is left adjoint to $G\mapsto(Q\mapsto G(X[Q]))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]; it is the specified $p_X^{-1}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Representables on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are sheaves by fpqc descent of maps [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The two adjunction/Yoneda bijections give $\operatorname{Hom}(p_X^{-1}h_P,G)=G(X[P])=\operatorname{Hom}(h_U,G)$. Here Yoneda is used in its full evaluation form [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]. The resulting isomorphism $p_X^{-1}h_P\cong h_U$ carries a generator indexed by $a:Q\to P$ and $b:V\to X[Q]$ to $X[a]b:V\to U$; the inverse is induced by the unit at $P$. Their composites fix the universal generator and hence are identities.

source.place: §3 preceding Example 3.1: p_X induced by profinite test objects; agent adjunction calculation

proof.text: Write $F_R$ for the free internal $R$-module functor on sheaves of sets. The free adjunction is the one defining $A=F_\Lambda(h_P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. The monoidal adjunction for $p_X^{-1}$ lifts to modules by [sk-def-sfb-transport], applied with $F=p_X^{-1}$ and $R=\Lambda$. For every $B$-module $M$, its adjunction followed by the free adjunction identifies maps $p_X^*F_\Lambda(h_P)\to M$ with maps $h_P\to p_{X,*}(UM)$, hence with maps $p_X^{-1}h_P\to UM$. Thus $p_X^*A$ has the defining universal property of $F_B(p_X^{-1}h_P)$, and step 1 gives $p_X^*A\cong B[h_U]$. These bijections send a linear map to its values on the unit generators, so the isomorphism preserves generators.

source.place: §3: pulled-back coefficient modules; agent free-adjunction calculation

proof.text: For a $B$-module sheaf $M$ and a test $V$, the sheaf Hom definition gives $\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],M)(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{B|_V}(B[h_U]|_V,M|_V)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The restricted free module is free on $h_U|_V$. Indeed, for $v:V\to X$, restriction of sheaves of sets and of abelian groups to $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V\simeq V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the inverse image $v^{-1}$ [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction, clause 1], left adjoint to $v_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; with the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_v$ the module pullback $v^*$ is restriction of $B$-modules [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization, sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], left adjoint to $v_*$, and $v_*$ commutes sectionwise with forgetting to sheaves of sets. Composing left adjoints as in step 2 gives $B[h_U]|_V\cong B|_V[h_U|_V]$, generators to generators; its sheafified presheaf model is that of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. In $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$ this parameter sheaf is represented by $V\times_XU\to V$, by the fibre-product universal property. Free adjunction and Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] therefore identify the displayed Hom with $M(V\times_XU)$. Explicitly a map $\phi$ goes to $\phi([\operatorname{pr}_U])$ on $V\times_XU$; a section $m$ goes to the linear map sending $[a:W\to U]$ to $(v_W,a)^*m$. These formulas are inverse, respect $B(V)$-multiplication and restriction along $V'\to V$, and commute with maps of $M$. This is an isomorphism of module sheaves, not an assertion that free sheaf sections are always free section modules.

The scheme $U=X[P]$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Its pro-etale site is the slice over $U$, using precisely the site-identification clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], not its constant-coefficient injectivity assertion. Under it the abelian inverse image $\rho^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is restriction to the slice and $\alpha_\rho:\rho^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}B\to B_U$ is a ring isomorphism [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization], so the module pullback $\rho^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_\rho}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(\rho^*_{\mathrm{Ab}})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] is $M\mapsto M|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $B_U$ acting through $\alpha_\rho$. It is exact: $\rho^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is the abelian inverse image along the base-change functor [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], exact by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], and extension along an isomorphism is an equivalence; so $L\rho^*=D(\rho^*)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Restriction is additive [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction-universes]. Choose a K-injective $J$ representing $K$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The universe-general restriction theorem [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-universes] shows $J|_U$ is K-injective. All its assumptions hold on the chosen small site: ordinary abelian sheafification and its local characterization are used, and restriction sends a zero map to zero sectionwise. Therefore $R\rho_*\rho^*K$ is represented by $\rho_*(J|_U)$, whose value at $V$ is $J(V\times_XU)$ by the direct-image definition [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and the K-injective definition of total direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. No boundedness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; preceding exact slice restriction and extension-by-zero discussion

proof.text: Use $B[h_U]$ concentrated in degree zero as the first representative. The K-injective model [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],K)$ by $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(B[h_U][0],J)$. The product Hom formula [def-pur-hom-complex] has only its $p=0$ factor nonzero, so its degree $n$ is $\mathcal Hom_B(B[h_U],J^n)$ and its differential is postcomposition by $d_J^n$. Apply the evaluation maps of step 3 in each degree. They give an actual chain isomorphism to $\rho_*(J|_U)$: on $V$ it is the identity of the complex $J(V\times_XU)$. Localizing this chain isomorphism and using steps 2 and 4 constructs $\gamma_{X,P,K}$. Each evaluation commutes with chain maps $J\to J'$, so it is natural on K-injective representatives and hence in the ordinary derived category. Independence of representatives is precisely the K-injective independence in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This gives the asserted differential and evaluation normalization on the whole derived object.

source.place: Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom: arbitrary first representative and K-injective second representative

proof.text: The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] leaves underlying sheaves, sections and maps unchanged. Its tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] sends $m\otimes n$ to the same local pure tensor. The derived Hom comparison [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] identifies the two Hom functors and their evaluation maps, also on every slice. Finally [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] identifies module pullback and direct image, with units and counits, under these exact equivalences. Applied termwise, an exact equivalence carries a K-injective complex to a K-injective complex: Hom from an acyclic complex identifies via its exact inverse with the original acyclic-Hom test. Consequently the direct-image models just used also identify. In particular the free generator $[a]$ and its evaluated value are unchanged on both sides, so these comparisons carry the constructed $\gamma$ to exactly the asserted internal-module isomorphism, with the required evaluation normalization.

source.place: Tag 08J7; agent application of the existing internal/section-module comparisons

proof.text: For $\rho:U\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] gives the canonical comparison $\rho^{-1}p_X^*\cong p_U^*$, including its lift to modules and the termwise derived functors. Apply this comparison to $N$ to obtain $\rho^*p_X^*N\cong p_U^*N$. It is the specified pullback-composition comparison, rather than an additional identification of coefficients.
